result: (13) इनशब्दस्येश्वरवाचकस्याकारलोपे सति नकारांतमिन्निति पदं भवति । दृ भय इति धातुः । स च परमेश्वरः शत्रूणां दारयिता भीषयितेतींद्रः ॥ (*inaśabdasyeśvaravācakasyākāralope sati nakārāṃtaminniti padaṃ bhavati | dṛ bhaya iti dhātuḥ | sa ca parameśvaraḥ śatrūṇāṃ dārayitā bhīṣayitetīṃdraḥ ‖*)—The word ina denotes the Lord. If the vowel a over the n of this word ina is dropped, the word in remains. The root dṛ⟨NOTE:10⟩ means fear. That god, the Supreme Lord, causes fear to enemies; hence the name Indra.

result: वृषस्व (*vṛṣasva*)—जठरे सिंच । यथा नाभेरधो न पतति तथा धारयेति भावः । (*jaṭhare siṃca | yathā nābheradho na patati tathā dhārayeti bhāvaḥ |*) In this verse it is plainly said पिब (*piba*), "drink the Soma juice"; is not the use of the word वृषस्व (*vṛṣasva*) then useless? The answer: since Indra is famous as extremely fond of drinking Soma juice, the use of the two words पिब (*piba*) and वृषस्व (*vṛṣasva*) ⟨NOTE:12⟩ is also proper, to stress plainly: "when drinking Soma, drink as much as you wish, so that it does not fall below the navel, and drink so that the inner part of the belly is well soaked and refreshed."

result: As the words of the Supreme Person say, उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोकाः न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहं (*utsīdeyurime lokāḥ na kuryāṃ karma cedahaṃ*)⟨NOTE:29⟩—"if I did not perform action, all the worlds would perish"—so, if Indra, the lord of the universe, were not constantly engaged in action useful for the conduct of the world, the ruin of the world would be certain. He is the cause of the appearance of Dawn and of the rising of the sun. As described in स्वराजः, महतः, ते (*svarājaḥ, mahataḥ, te*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-1), he alone is lord of the whole universe and holds sovereign rank. Even so, because the performance of sacrifice nourishes the world and is the cause of the growth of prosperity of the whole world, of gods, men and others, it is said that Indra honoured Dawn and the Sun, the primary causes of that sacrifice. The purport of the present Ṛk is that, though himself the lord, he worshipped his own creation, which nourishes the world.

result: ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—This epithet is because he is accompanied by Soma. It is used chiefly in describing the nature of Indra and the Maruts. In such contexts as "अमत्रेभिर्ऋजीषिणिमिंद्रं (*amatrebhirṛjīṣiṇimiṃdraṃ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-42-2) ⟨NOTE:36⟩ the word ṛjīṣa is explained as power; it is explained as "of Indra, who has obtained power that obstructs enemies". But in many contexts this epithet is well known precisely because he is accompanied by Soma.

result: The Ṛk ये त्वाहिहत्ये (*ye tvāhihatye*) is the yājyā in the Marutvatīya śastra. It is prescribed by the sūtra ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या (*ye tvāhihatye maghavannavardhanniti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-14). O Maghavan Indra, the Maruts who in the work of slaying Ahi (Vṛtra) strengthened you by giving you strength, with words such as "strike, blessed one, slay, show your valour"; and, O Harivān (possessor of horses) Indra, those who strengthened you in the battle connected with the slaying of Śambara. That Indra slew Śambara is stated by a mantra passage: यः शंबरं पर्वतेषु क्षियंतं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविंदत् । ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान । (*yaḥ śaṃbaraṃ parvateṣu kṣiyaṃtaṃ catvāriṃśyāṃ śaradyanvaviṃdat | ojāyamānaṃ yo ahiṃ jaghāna |*) (Ṛ.
